featured_reviews.review_text:
Shameful & Disturbing Incident Outside Mani’s, Mulund (18th Oct 2025)
This review isn’t about food — it’s about basic humanity, which I saw completely missing outside Mani’s, Mulund West on the evening of 18th October 2025 (Saturday) during Diwali time.
While I was having dosa with my family, I witnessed something horrifying — a tall man in a kurta slapped and dragged a young beggar girl right outside the café. She must have been barely 10–12 years old. He hit her so hard, then grabbed her by her t-shirt and pulled her, while everyone just stood there and watched. It was one of the most disgusting things I’ve ever seen.
And what shocked me most — not one single person from Mani’s staff or management came forward. No one tried to stop that man or even check on that child. Everyone simply ignored it as if nothing happened. Even after assaulting her, that man came back to collect his parcel calmly while his wife sat in the car watching!
I want to ask Mani’s management — do your CCTV cameras not work? Did no staff member see this? Why didn’t anyone step up? It happened right at your doorstep. If you claim to be a family-friendly place, you also have a moral responsibility to protect people outside your premises, especially a child being assaulted in public view.
That moment made me lose all respect for this place. Good food means nothing when basic humanity and courage are missing. I truly hope Mani’s management takes this seriously, checks their CCTV footage from 18th October, identifies that man, and at least reports this inhuman act. Silence in such situations is shameful.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Sindhudurg Family Dining to celebrate a birthday, and overall it was a mixed experience.

The restaurant is very conveniently located, especially for people coming from Mulund East railway station. The management is also supportive for small celebrations like birthdays, so that’s a plus.

However, the space is quite compact with tight seating. It can feel a bit congested, and there’s definitely room for improvement in terms of space management and comfort.

Service is another area that needs attention. There was noticeable delay in serving orders, and it seemed to be a common issue across tables, not just ours.

Coming to food:

Starters like Bombil Fry, Crab Lollipop, and Chicken Tikka Kebab were good in taste. The Crab Lollipop was the highlight.

We tried Rawas and Surmai Thalis. Surmai was fresh and tasty, while Rawas was just average. The fish curry in the thali was quite bland.

Prawns Malvani Masala and Pomfret Tawa Fry were disappointing. The prawns dish had an overpowering coconut taste, and the pomfret didn’t feel very fresh.

Chicken Sukha was flavorful and well-prepared, but Kombdi Vade didn’t feel authentic—it was more like a puri.

Surmai Tawa Fry (ordered later) was again very good.

Solkadhi was impressive and better than many nearby seafood places.

One more thing to note is the portion size—it felt a bit less for the price, so overall it came across as slightly expensive for the quantity served.

Overall, it’s a decent place for seafood with some really good dishes, but consistency, authenticity, service speed, and portion sizing need improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Author Kailash amesur

I recently dined at Azad Pure Veg Restaurant, a place I’ve long anticipated visiting. Years ago, this spot was celebrated for serving the best Vada Pav in Mulund. I used to stop by occasionally for a bite of that delicious snack, and now, it has transformed into a full-fledged restaurant.

Upon entering, I was impressed by the well-maintained ambiance and clever space management. The restaurant offers both air-conditioned and non-AC seating areas, catering to different preferences. The cleanliness and hygiene standards are commendable, which is always a plus for any dining experience.

We ordered a Manchurian starter and sizzlers, and I was pleasantly surprised by the generous portions. Unlike many other places where you find yourself searching for the cooked portion of sizzler, Azad serves a substantial amount of noodles and rice, along with a delightful paneer gravy. They also add a refreshing salad and crispy fries to the plate, making it a hearty meal.

What struck me the most was the overall value for money. The dishes we ordered were both economical and incredibly tasty. If you're weary of overpriced, exotic meals, Azad Pure Veg is a fantastic spot for enjoying traditional food with family or friends.

In conclusion, Azad Pure Veg Restaurant is a delightful place that marries nostalgia with a modern dining experience. Whether you’re craving some comfort food or looking for a hygienic and spacious restaurant to share a meal with loved ones, this place is definitely worth a visit. I highly recommend it!

featured_reviews.name: Neeraj Savant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Thambbi Veg Restaurant – Mulund West

If you’re looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian cuisine in Mulund, Thambbi Veg Restaurant is a must-visit. This place serves up a delightful variety of traditional dishes that are packed with flavor and made with care.

We started with their Paper Dosa, which truly lived up to its name—crisp, golden, and impressively long. It’s perfect for dosa lovers! Another crowd favorite here is the Andhra Masala Dosa, known for its spicy, flavorful filling that sets it apart from the usual masala dosa.

The South Indian Thali was wholesome and satisfying, offering a variety of classic items that balance each other perfectly. We also tried the Ragi Idli, a healthy yet tasty option that’s soft and light. Every dish was accompanied by fresh chutneys and piping hot sambar, both of which were incredibly flavorful and clearly made fresh.

A highlight of the meal was their strong, aromatic Filter Kaapi, served the traditional way—perfect to wrap up a hearty meal. And for dessert, the Payasam was rich, comforting, and not overly sweet—just right.

What made the experience even better was the courteous and attentive staff, who ensured we were comfortable and served promptly despite the busy crowd. The ambience is simple but clean and welcoming, suitable for both quick meals and family outings.

Overall, Thambbi offers a truly satisfying South Indian dining experience that delivers on taste, authenticity, and hospitality. Highly recommended for anyone craving comforting, vegetarian South Indian food in the heart of Mulund.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Dhonde
featured_reviews.review_text:
TFT Mulund: Beautiful Ambience, Average Food, Poor Hospitality

Last night, we visited Mulund’s The Food Town (TFT) to celebrate wife’s birthday and make it a truly memorable occasion.

On the culinary side, the Mushroom Soup was delicious and well-prepared, while the Mexican Sizzler, though served average hot, was only average in taste. The Avocado Sushi too felt quite ordinary, lacking the flavor one would expect. When we ordered the Sizzler Brownie with Ice Cream, we were informed that the ice cream was melting, compelling us to cancel. Overall, the food quality and presentation were below expectations.

However, what left us most disappointed was the lack of warmth and sensitivity in hospitality. Despite TFT having three beautifully decorated side tables, which could have made our special day more memorable with photographs, our request to be relocated was denied. The waiter directed us to Mr. Vivek Asthana, who, instead of showing flexibility or customer empathy, flatly refused stating that the tables were reserved for larger groups—even though one such table remained vacant throughout our visit (as seen in the attached photograph). Ironically, another table with only three guests was being used, raising questions about consistency in policy.

When I suggested that hospitality should prioritize enhancing the experience of guests already present rather than waiting for potential walk-ins, Mr. Asthana maintained his refusal. This rigid approach not only dampened the spirit of our celebration but also raised concerns about the basic principles of guest satisfaction and service etiquette.

Towards the end, a group of teenagers entered, creating a noisy, chaotic, fish-market-like atmosphere that ruined the dining vibe. After informing,  though Mr. Asthana later shifted them, the overall experience was already compromised.

Frankly, I am unable to understand why Mr. Vivek Asthana chose to keep a table vacant rather than allow a genuine guest to create memories on a special occasion.

Is this truly what modern hospitality management teaches—denial over delight, rigidity over responsiveness, and policy over people?

featured_reviews.name: Krisha Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Krishna Bhog NX is a well-known spot for vegetarian food, offering a decent variety of dishes that cater well to family dining and casual meals. The menu has a good mix of North Indian and basic Indian comfort food options, and the taste overall feels satisfying, especially for those who prefer simple, homely flavours.

The food quality is generally good, with fresh preparation and decent portion sizes. Many dishes are flavorful and well-presented, making it a nice option for dine-in or ordering when you are in the mood for vegetarian cuisine.

However, the biggest concern is the service experience. The staff is polite, but the service is quite slow and there seems to be a delay in managing orders efficiently. The waiting time for food is longer than expected, which can be frustrating during busy hours.

In addition, the food arriving time was very late, which affects the overall dining experience. Even after ordering, there is a noticeable delay in serving, so it is recommended to visit only when you have enough time to wait. With better service speed and improved order management, Krishna Bhog NX can definitely offer a much better experience.

It's located on the first floor and you may be required to use a small lift besides the Hari Om shop. It also has a small banquet to host small functions. The menu has all the dishes from south to north indian cuisines.

featured_reviews.name: Niyati Pandya
featured_reviews.review_text: It's my favourite place. I loved this place since my college days. Firstly I am love with their samosas. It's the ultimate and same taste since my college days probably 10 years. Hariom  started with their sweet and farsan and now they have opened food court. Right from hygiene and food they will never disappoint. I highly highly recommend to try this place. Hariom food court serves all the cuisine in one place. Right from pavbhaji , pasta ,pizza ,chinese ,juices and much more. This is a complete family restaurant and quantity wise it serves 2-3people. I have tried their sweets, farsan and food every thing is very good with good quality. Do try this place.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited this food court and the first impression was It's Clean!
This place has everything! Beautiful and warm atmosphere, Well trained staff, quick service and Food is good too. Ordered a couple of Sandwiches and they were delicious. (American Cheese and corn grill , Pahadi grill)
White/Alfredo Pasta is Outstanding.
Chinese starters could have been better. We ordered spring rolls and veg crispy, both were average.
For desert we opted for sizzling brownie.
Overall it was a great experience.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you so much for your very kind words. We are all delighted that you liked the Food, Ambience and our Service.It was a privilege having you, and I hope we can do it again soon.

featured_reviews.name: Sunita Deulkar
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited this food court expecting it too be small and like normal food court. But was surprised to see big dining space and fine dine experience. Ambience, Service, Food variety and food taste.. everything was good. Looking forward for many visits.. finally restaurant with big space in Mulund east.

Hi Sunita,
We are glad you enjoyed your time at our foodcourt. We are always striving to serve you better and are looking forward to your next visit

featured_reviews.name: Sharad Kambale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great food, good ambience but service felt a bit lacking.
Came here for dinner and initially a Waiter took our order. To start with we ordered 2 starters and a drinks. After about 5 mins another staff came to take our order digitally. We calmly repeated the order not sure if the waiter earlier had placed the order or not. The 2 starters came quickly but the drink did not. The drink, a simple sweet lime soda came after all 4 dishes came to our table. Disappoting. It was for the kid.

Pretty much all the dishes were good. Sichuan chilli paneer, Pita Platter, Mexican Pizza and Khau Suey. Pita platter had way too many dips which go waste as the bread finishes earlier. The dips need to be proportional to the bread.

Khau Suey was stellar. But the waiter did a very sloppy job of preparing the individual Khau Suey bowls with the curry dripping on all sides of the bowl. This is not expected in this day and age. We are in a fine dining setup not some road side stall.

The other issue we faced was that while we were dining the waiter tried to pick up the dips even though we weren't done. He did not even bother asking. I'll put it down to new staff.

But a couple of incidents in a short span of time aren't a good impression.

Service needs improvement even though the food is great.

featured_reviews.name: Bhakti Menon
featured_reviews.review_text: Although the ambience is good, the food is strictly ok. The portion size is good but the taste is not authentic. The service really has to improve as the servers actually hover over your tables. We ordered appetizers and main course and everything just came together. The least we expect is a fine dine restaurant should know to serve dishes in proper order. Our server spilled rice thrice while serving. For the pricing, the restaurant offers very mediocre service.

featured_reviews.name: shreyash kothari
featured_reviews.review_text: Very bad experience wrt food taste and hygiene.  Water bottles are of plastic with fungus and food taste is not at all good. Needs improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Ketan Astik
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food is just about average for the price they charge almost everything is in north of ₹300. Portion too is average.
Staff is completely untrained. You ask them something and they would run around like headless chicken. I celebrated a birthday there and they said they do not give service on the table kept outside. And even after paying a 5 figure bill, they couldnt give me 10 carry boxes to give away the cake. They charged me for that too..

featured_reviews.name: Rakesh Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Thyme & Whisk in Mulund recently. Tried the Avocado Roll Sushi, Smokey Three Lasagne, Mongolian Toss Up Sizzler, and Tiramisu. The sizzler was tasty and served in good quantity, but the sushi was quite bland. Overall, I found the dishes a bit overpriced for what they offer.

The restaurant is located inside Kalidas Hall, which is not very easy to find if you’re coming for the first time. Ambience is simple and doesn’t really match the pictures online. Personally, I feel Food Town nearby is a better choice.

Also worth noting: the 7% service tax on the bill is optional and can be removed if you ask.

featured_reviews.name: Boskee Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
🍽️ Chappan Bhog Thali Restaurant

There are meals… and then there are experiences that sit quietly in your heart long after the table is cleared. ✨

Just visited Chappan Bhog Thali Restaurant for their newly launched Aamras Festival, and I have to say, this was mango season done right.

The Aamras? Unbelievably fresh. The kind that tastes like it was poured straight from a sun kissed orchard. Usually early season mangoes hold back a little. This one did not. It was rich, silky, naturally sweet, and absolutely unadulterated. No artificial aftertaste. Just pure mango magic 🥭✨
And the thali… every single element carried authentic flavour. Not a single dish felt rushed or overpowering. The spices were beautifully balanced, allowing each preparation to shine without competing for attention. From sabzis to farsan to sweets, everything tasted like it came from a kitchen that respects tradition.

Service was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. The staff ensured refills were generous and timely without hovering. That rare balance that makes you feel looked after but relaxed.

The ambience deserves its own applause. Calm, elegant, and soul soothing. Perfect for a family lunch, festive outing, or simply indulging in comfort food that feels like home but elevated.

If you love authentic thali experiences and want to start mango season on the sweetest possible note, their Aamras Festival is not to be missed.

Soul satisfying food. Soul soothing vibe. And Aamras that sets the bar dangerously high for the rest of the season. 🥭✨

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Joshi
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a delightful meal here! 😋 The thali was flavorful and diverse, a true treat. 🍲 The ambiance was truly wonderful, creating a perfect setting. ✨ Service was adequate, but could be a bit more attentive. Definitely worth a visit for the food and atmosphere! 💯

featured_reviews.name: Candy Coated Cravings
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Chhappan Bhog for their unlimited aamras thali priced at ₹599. The ambiance and variety were definitely good, but the food lacked flavour overall. Most dishes were very mild and less spicy, which personally didn’t work for me. Expected a much tastier experience for the price, so probably wouldn’t visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Sayli Satam
featured_reviews.review_text:
5/5 Stars: A Culinary Delight!

I recently had the pleasure of dining at this amazing restaurant, and I'm still drooling over the experience! The food is truly awesome, with an incredible variety of options, including half Jain dishes. What caught my attention were the special dishes - the sweets, jalebi, and daal baati were absolute showstoppers! Each bite was a flavor explosion that left me wanting more.

- *Quality Food*: Fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection.
- *Variety*: Impressive options, including half Jain dishes, to cater to different tastes.
- *Specialties*: Sweets, jalebi, and daal baati are must-try dishes that will tantalize your taste buds.
- *Ambience*: The restaurant's atmosphere is warm and inviting, perfect for a night out with family or friends.
- *Service*: The staff is attentive, courteous, and efficient - hats off to them!

- Don't miss out on their special desserts - they're heavenly!
- The restaurant's menu is diverse, so you're sure to find something that suits your taste.
- The service is top-notch, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

If you're a foodie like me, this place is a must-visit. Trust me, you won't regret it!
